nodes.name: NiFe foam cleaning
nodes.procedure: A piece of NiFe foam (1 × 0.5 m) was washed with ethanol several times to clean the surface for further use.
nodes.source_text: A piece of NiFe foam (1 × 0.5 m) was washed with ethanol several times to clean the surface for further use.

nodes.name: Room-temperature immersion sulfuration
nodes.procedure: Ferric chloride hexahydrate (2.8 kg) and sodium thiosulfate (0.2 kg) were dissolved in 30 L of water, and the mixture was then stirred vigorously to form a transparent solution. The cleaned NiFe foam (Ni:Fe = 4:6, 1 × 0.5 m) was submerged into the solution for 1 h with constant stirring. After washing with deionized water, the (Ni,Fe)3S2 nanosheets were achieved on NiFe foam.

nodes.name: Hydrothermal Ni3S2 synthesis
nodes.procedure: According to the previously reported method, a piece of Ni foam (2 × 4 cm) was immersed into 67 mL of water containing thioureas (1.1 g) in a Teflon autoclave. The autoclave was sealed and maintained at 150 °C for 5 h in an oven. The resulting material was washed with water three times and dried at room temperature, giving Ni3S2/NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern of (Ni,Fe)₃S₂/NFF shows diffraction peaks of metallic nickel/iron and heazlewoodite phase Ni₃S₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of (Ni,Fe)₃S₂/NFF in Figure 2a shows that in addition to the diffraction peaks of metallic nickel/iron, a set of diffraction peaks are indexed to heazlewoodite phase Ni₃S₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra of (Ni,Fe)₃S₂/NFF exhibit characteristic Raman bands of Ni₃S₂ at 223, 304, 324, and 350 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra of (Ni,Fe)₃S₂/NFF (Figure 2b) also exhibit the characteristic Raman bands of Ni₃S₂ at 223, 304, 324, and 350 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show (Ni,Fe)₃S₂/NFF maintains 3D macroporous structure of NFF with entire surface homogeneously coated by vertically grown (Ni,Fe)₃S₂ nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM images of (Ni,Fe)₃S₂/NFF present that the 3D macroporous structure of NFF stays intact in (Ni,Fe)₃S₂/NFF ... and that the entire NFF surface is homogeneously coated by the vertically grown (Ni,Fe)₃S₂ nanosheets with a smooth surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM image confirms uniform nanosheet morphology of (Ni,Fe)₃S₂ with thickness ≈2-10 nm on NFF surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image and scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) image confirms the uniform nanosheet morphology of (Ni,Fe)₃S₂ (Figure 2c,d). The thickness of (Ni,Fe)₃S₂ is ≈2-10 nm on the NFF surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM image and elemental mapping indicate homogeneous distribution of Fe, Ni, and S elements on (Ni,Fe)₃S₂/NFF surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM elemental mapping analysis (Figure 2d) indicates the homogeneous distribution of Fe, Ni, and S elements on the surface of (Ni,Fe)₃S₂/NFF.

properties.description: Elemental mapping image with scale bar 50 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS analysis confirms Ni:Fe atomic ratio of 5.5:1 in (Ni,Fe)₃S₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic ratio of Ni:Fe is 5.5:1, as confirmed by energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) analysis (Figure S6, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows lattice spacings of 0.29 nm and 0.24 nm corresponding to (003) and (110) planes of (Ni,Fe)₃S₂ basal plane, and 0.25 nm for (220) plane at folded edge.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Two distinct lattice spacings of 0.29 and 0.24 nm are observed in the basal plane (Figure 2e), corresponding to the (003) and (110) crystal planes of the (Ni,Fe)₃S₂ ... HRTEM image of the folded edge shows a lattice spacing of 0.25 nm (Figure 2f), which is assigned to the (220) crystal plane of (Ni,Fe)₃S₂ nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution Ni 2p, Fe 2p, and S 2p XPS spectra show Ni³⁺ and Fe³⁺ states on (Ni,Fe)₃S₂/NFF surface (vs mixed Ni⁰/Ni³⁺ and Fe⁰/Fe³⁺ on NFF); S 2p peaks at 163.0 and 164.4 eV attributed to S²⁻.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2g-i exhibits high-resolution Ni 2p, Fe 2p, and S 2p XPS spectra of (Ni,Fe)₃S₂/NFF and the reference samples (NFF). The mixed valence states (i.e., Ni⁰/Ni³⁺ and Fe⁰/Fe³⁺) exist on NFF surface ... Unlike the NFF, the nickel and iron on (Ni,Fe)₃S₂/NFF surface exist only as Ni³⁺ and Fe³⁺. In the high-resolution S 2p XPS spectra (Figure 2i), the peaks at 163.0 and 164.4 eV are attributed to S²⁻ in (Ni,Fe)₃S₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman during HER (0 to -85 mV vs RHE) shows characteristic peaks of (Ni,Fe)₃S₂ at 221, 304, 324, and 351 cm⁻¹ remain unchanged.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 4a illustrates that the characteristic peaks of (Ni,Fe)₃S₂ including 221(Eg), 304(Eg), 324(Ag), and 351 cm⁻¹(Eg) remain unchanged across a range of reduction potentials from 0 to 85 mV.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman during OER (1.23 to 1.44 V vs RHE) shows transformation from (Ni,Fe)₃S₂ to Ni(OH)₂ then to γ-(Ni,Fe)OOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the potential range of 1.23 to 1.35 V, the intensities of (Ni,Fe)₃S₂ characteristic peaks exhibit a diminishing trend, accompanied by the emergence of new Raman bands near 460 and 530 cm⁻¹ ... At voltages between 1.35 and 1.36 V, two new Raman bands near 470 and 550 cm⁻¹ are attributed to Eg bending vibration of Ni-O bands and A1g stretching vibration of Ni-O bands for γ-NiOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ICP-OES shows low leaching contents of S, Fe, and Ni during HER; higher S leaching than Fe/Ni during OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ inductively coupled plasma-optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) confirms that the leaching contents of S, Fe, and Ni are very low (Figure S15, Supporting Information) ... The total leaching concentration of S ions is significantly higher than that of Fe and Ni ions.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER XPS shows no S signals, O 1s peaks at 530.7 eV (Ni/Fe-O), 531.5 eV (Ni/Fe-OH), 532.5 eV (adsorbed water); Ni and Fe both in +3 oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS spectrum of (Ni,Fe)₃S₂/NFF after OER (Figure S19a, Supporting Information) presents no signals corresponding to S atoms ... The O 1s spectrum of (Ni,Fe)₃S₂/NFF after OER (Figure 5e) could be deconvoluted into three peaks, namely Ni/Fe-O (530.7 eV), Ni/Fe-OH (531.5 eV), and adsorbed water (532.5 eV) ... In Ni 2p and Fe 2p XPS spectra of (Ni,Fe)₃S₂/NFF after OER (Figure S19b,c, Supporting Information), both the oxidation state of Ni and Fe atoms are +3.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER HRTEM shows no lattice fringes, indicating amorphous surface of transformed catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: No lattice fringes are observed in the HRTEM image of (Ni,Fe)₃S₂/NFF after OER (Figure 5d), suggesting an amorphous surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER EDS shows surface Ni:Fe atomic ratio of 7.4:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The surface atomic ratio of Ni to Fe is 7.4:1 for the (Ni,Fe)₃S₂/NFF after OER, as revealed by the EDS analysis (Figure S20, Supporting Information).
